title: Milan: GATED - treadmill incline if walking is clean, otherwise bike
terrain: treadmill 10-12% incline (climbing only) or indoor bike, zero descent either way

steps.target: Z2 at 10-12% incline or bike Z2, 80-88% LTHR

coachNotes: THE GATE: run this on the treadmill ONLY if you have walked for a full 24 hours with no pin sensations at all. Anything at all, even once, and today is the bike again at the same load. Do not average the day out in your head, one pin is a fail. WHY UPHILL IS THE EXCEPTION. If running comes back this week it comes back on a steep treadmill and nowhere else. ITBS is provoked by the knee cycling repeatedly through roughly 20-30 degrees of flexion under load, which is what flat running and especially downhill running do. Steep uphill running keeps the knee outside that band for most of the stride and has no eccentric braking phase at all, so it is the one running modality that buys fitness without paying the band. Hold 10-12%, let the pace be whatever it needs to be, walk the belt if that is what the gradient demands. ABORT RULE: any pin, twinge or lateral knee sensation during the run, step off immediately and finish on the bike. This is not a test of tolerance, we already know the band is talking. It is a test of whether uphill is available to us. NO GYM TODAY, legs recover between the hip blocks. GUT TRAINING CONTINUES REGARDLESS OF MODALITY: 80 g/h means 2 Enervit Carbo Gel C2:1 Pro per hour (40g each, 2:1 glucose-fructose) with 150-250ml of water per gel. Today is 55 minutes so take one gel at minute 30. The bike is a perfectly good place to train a gut, so this part of the week is untouched by the ITB.
